o: Y así, fatigado deste pensamiento, abrevió su venteril y limitada cena; la cual acabada, llamó al ventero, y, encerrándose con él en la caballeriza, se hincó de rodillas ante él, diciéndole.
t: And so, worn out by this thought, he shortened his meager and scanty supper; and once it was finished, he called the innkeeper, and, shutting himself up with him in the stable, he knelt before him, saying:

o: — No me levantaré jamás de donde estoy, valeroso caballero, fasta que la vuestra cortesía me otorgue un don que pedirle quiero, el cual redundará en alabanza vuestra y en pro del género humano.
t: "I will never rise from where I am, valorous knight, until your courtesy grants me a boon I wish to ask, which will redound to your praise and to the benefit of the human race."

o: El ventero, que vio a su huésped a sus pies y oyó semejantes razones, estaba confuso mirándole, sin saber qué hacerse ni decirle, y porfiaba con él que se levantase, y jamás quiso, hasta que le hubo de decir que él le otorgaba el don que le pedía.
t: The innkeeper, who saw his guest at his feet and heard such words, was bewildered, staring at him, not knowing what to do or say, and he urged him to get up, and he would not, until the innkeeper had to tell him that he granted him the boon he asked for.

o: Preguntóle si traía dineros; respondió don Quijote que no traía blanca, porque él nunca había leído en las historias de los caballeros andantes que ninguno los hubiese traído.
t: He asked him if he had any money; Don Quixote replied that he had not a penny, because he had never read in the histories of knights-errant that any of them had ever carried money.

o: Contó el ventero a todos cuantos estaban en la venta la locura de su huésped, la vela de las armas y la armazón de caballería que esperaba.
t: The innkeeper told everyone in the inn the madness of his guest, the polishing of the armor, and the knightly harness he was expecting.

o: Admiráronse de tan estraño género de locura y fuéronselo a mirar desde lejos, y vieron que, con sosegado ademán, unas veces se paseaba; otras, arrimado a su lanza, ponía los ojos en las armas, sin quitarlos por un buen espacio dellas.
t: They marveled at such a strange kind of madness and went to watch him from a distance, and they saw that, with a calm demeanor, sometimes he strolled about; at other times, leaning on his lance, he fixed his eyes on the armor, not taking them off it for a good while.

o: Acabó de cerrar la noche, pero con tanta claridad de la luna, que podía competir con el que se la prestaba, de manera que cuanto el novel caballero hacía era bien visto de todos.
t: Night closed in, but so bright was the moonlight that it could compete with the sun that lent it, so that everything the new knight did was clearly seen by all.

o: Antojósele en esto a uno de los arrieros que estaban en la venta ir a dar agua a su recua, y fue menester quitar las armas de don Quijote, que estaban sobre la pila; el cual, viéndole llegar, en voz alta le dijo.
t: It occurred to one of the muleteers who were in the inn to go and give water to his pack animals, and it was necessary to remove Don Quixote's armor, which lay on the trough; and when the muleteer saw him coming, he said aloud:

o: — ¡Oh tú, quienquiera que seas, atrevido caballero, que llegas a tocar las armas del más valeroso andante que jamás se ciñó espada!, mira lo que haces y no las toques, si no quieres dejar la vida en pago de tu atrevimiento.
t: "Oh you, whoever you are, bold knight, who come to lay hands on the armor of the most valorous knight-errant that ever girded on a sword! Look what you are doing and do not touch it, unless you wish to leave your life as the price of your boldness."

o: No se curó el arriero destas razones (y fuera mejor que se curara, porque fuera curarse en salud); antes, trabando de las correas, las arrojó gran trecho de sí.
t: The muleteer paid no heed to these words (and it would have been better if he had, for it is better to be cured in health); on the contrary, seizing the straps, he threw the armor a good distance away from him.

o: Lo cual visto por don Quijote, alzó los ojos al cielo, y, puesto el pensamiento —a lo que pareció— en su señora Dulcinea, dijo.
t: Which, seen by Don Quixote, he lifted his eyes to heaven, and, setting his thoughts — as it seemed — on his lady Dulcinea, he said:

o: — Acorredme, señora mía, en esta primera afrenta que a este vuestro avasallado pecho se le ofrece; no me desfallezca en este primero trance vuestro favor y amparo.
t: "Help me, my lady, in this first affront offered to this your enslaved breast; let not your favor and protection fail me in this first moment."

o: Y, diciendo estas y otras semejantes razones, soltando la adarga, alzó la lanza a dos manos y dio con ella tan gran golpe al arriero en la cabeza, que le derribó en el suelo, tan maltrecho que, si segundara con otro, no tuviera necesidad de maestro que le curara.
t: And, saying these and other similar words, he let go of the strap, raised the lance with both hands, and dealt the muleteer such a blow on the head that he knocked him to the ground so battered that, had he followed up with another, he would have had no need of a surgeon to cure him.

o: Hecho esto, recogió sus armas y tornó a pasearse con el mismo reposo que primero.
t: Having done this, he gathered up his armor and began to stroll about again with the same composure as before.

o: Al ruido acudió toda la gente de la venta, y entre ellos el ventero.
t: At the noise the whole crowd in the inn came running, and among them the innkeeper.

o: Viendo esto don Quijote, embrazó su adarga, y, puesta mano a su espada, dijo.
t: Seeing this, Don Quixote grabbed his shield, and, setting his hand to his sword, said:

o: — ¡Oh señora de la fermosura, esfuerzo y vigor del debilitado corazón mío!
t: "Oh lady of beauty, strength, and vigor of my weakened heart!"

o: Ahora es tiempo que vuelvas los ojos de tu grandeza a este tu cautivo caballero, que tamaña aventura está atendiendo.
t: Now is the time to turn the eyes of your greatness upon this captive knight of yours, who awaits so great an adventure.

o: Con esto cobró, a su parecer, tanto ánimo, que si le acometieran todos los arrieros del mundo, no volviera el pie atrás.
t: With this he gathered, as it seemed to him, so much courage that if all the muleteers in the world were to come at him, he would not have retreated a single step.

o: Los compañeros de los heridos, que tales los vieron, comenzaron desde lejos a llover piedras sobre don Quijote, el cual, lo mejor que podía, se reparaba con su adarga, y no se osaba apartar de la pila por no desamparar las armas.
t: The companions of the wounded men, seeing them thus, began from a distance to rain stones upon Don Quixote, who defended himself as best he could with his shield, and did not dare to move away from the pile for fear of abandoning the arms.

o: El ventero daba voces que le dejasen, porque ya les había dicho como era loco, y que por loco se libraría, aunque los matase a todos.
t: The innkeeper was shouting that they should leave him alone, because he had already told them he was mad, and that on account of his madness he would go free, even if they killed them all.

o: También don Quijote las daba, mayores, llamándolos de alevosos y traidores, y que el señor del castillo era un follón y mal nacido caballero, pues de tal manera consentía que se tratasen los andantes caballeros; y que si él hubiera recebido la orden de caballería, que él le diera a entender su alevosía.
t: Don Quixote was shouting too, louder still, calling them rascals and traitors, and saying that the lord of the castle was a knave and a low-born knight, since he consented in such a way to the mistreatment of knights-errant; and that if he had received the order of knighthood, he would have taught him a lesson for his villainy.

o: — Pero de vosotros, soez y baja canalla, no hago caso alguno: tirad, llegad, venid y ofendedme en cuanto pudiéredes, que vosotros veréis el pago que lleváis de vuestra sandez y demasía.
t: "But of you, base and vulgar rabble, I make no account at all: throw, come on, approach and offend me as much as you are able, and you shall see the payment you will get for your folly and insolence."

o: Decía esto con tanto brío y denuedo, que infundió un terrible temor en los que le acometían; y, así por esto como por las persuasiones del ventero, le dejaron de tirar, y él dejó retirar a los heridos y tornó a la vela de sus armas con la misma quietud y sosiego que primero.
t: He said this with such spirit and boldness that he inspired a terrible fear in those who were assailing him; and both for this reason and because of the innkeeper's persuasions, they stopped throwing stones, and he let the wounded men be carried off and returned to the care of his arms with the same calm and composure as at first.

o: No le parecieron bien al ventero las burlas de su huésped, y determinó abreviar y darle la negra orden de caballería luego, antes que otra desgracia sucediese.
t: The innkeeper did not care for his guest's jests, and resolved to cut short the matter and give him the black order of knighthood right away, before some further misfortune occurred.

o: Y así, llegándose a él, se desculpó de la insolencia que aquella gente baja con él había usado, sin que él supiese cosa alguna; pero que bien castigados quedaban de su atrevimiento.
t: And so, coming up to him, he excused the insolence that that base rabble had used toward him, though he knew nothing of it; but that they were already well punished for their boldness.

o: Todo se lo creyó don Quijote, y dijo que él estaba allí pronto para obedecerle, y que concluyese con la mayor brevedad que pudiese; porque si fuese otra vez acometido y se viese armado caballero, no pensaba dejar persona viva en el castillo, eceto aquellas que él le mandase, a quien por su respeto dejaría.
t: Don Quixote believed it all, and said that he was there ready to obey him, and that he should conclude with the greatest brevity he could; because if he were attacked again and found himself dubbed a knight, he did not intend to leave a single person alive in the castle, except those whom he should command, whom he would spare out of respect.

o: Hecho esto, mandó a una de aquellas damas que le ciñese la espada, la cual lo hizo con mucha desenvoltura y discreción, porque no fue menester poca para no reventar de risa a cada punto de las ceremonias; pero las proezas que ya habían visto del novel caballero les tenía la risa a raya.
t: This done, he ordered one of those ladies to gird his sword, which she did with great ease and discretion, for it took no little effort not to burst out laughing at every point of the ceremony; but the feats they had already seen from the new knight kept their laughter in check.

o: Al ceñirle la espada, dijo la buena señora.
t: When she girded on his sword, the good lady said:

o: — Dios haga a vuestra merced muy venturoso caballero y le dé ventura en lides.
t: "May God make your grace a very fortunate knight and grant you good fortune in your battles."

o: Don Quijote le preguntó cómo se llamaba, porque él supiese de allí adelante a quién quedaba obligado por la merced recebida; porque pensaba darle alguna parte de la honra que alcanzase por el valor de su brazo.
t: Don Quixote asked her name, so that from then on he might know to whom he was bound by the favor received; for he meant to give her some share of the honor he might win through the valor of his arm.

o: Ella respondió con mucha humildad que se llamaba la Tolosa, y que era hija de un remendón natural de Toledo que vivía a las tendillas de Sancho Bienaya, y que dondequiera que ella estuviese le serviría y le tendría por señor.
t: She replied with much humility that her name was la Tolosa, and that she was the daughter of a native mender of Toledo who lived at the stalls of Sancho Bienaya, and that wherever she might be, she would serve him and hold him as her lord.

o: Don Quijote le replicó que, por su amor, le hiciese merced que de allí adelante se pusiese don y se llamase doña Tolosa.
t: Don Quixote replied that, for her love's sake, he would ask her the favor that from then on she would take the title of don and be called doña Tolosa.

o: Ella se lo prometió, y la otra le calzó la espuela, con la cual le pasó casi el mismo coloquio que con la de la espada: preguntóle su nombre, y dijo que se llamaba la Molinera, y que era hija de un honrado molinero de Antequera; a la cual también rogó don Quijote que se pusiese don y se llamase doña Molinera, ofreciéndole nuevos servicios y mercedes.
t: She promised him this, and the other one buckled on his spur, and with her held almost the same conversation as the one with the sword: he asked her name, and she said she was called la Molinera, and that she was the daughter of an honest miller of Antequera; and Don Quixote likewise begged her to take the title of don and be called doña Molinera, offering her new services and favors.

o: Hechas, pues, de galope y aprisa las hasta allí nunca vistas ceremonias, no vio la hora don Quijote de verse a caballo y salir buscando las aventuras; y, ensillando luego a Rocinante, subió en él, y, abrazando a su huésped, le dijo cosas tan estrañas, agradeciéndole la merced de haberle armado caballero, que no es posible acertar a referirlas.
t: The ceremonies, hitherto never seen, having thus been done in a rush and hastily, Don Quixote could hardly wait the hour to find himself on horseback and go forth in search of adventures; and, saddling Rocinante at once, he mounted him and, embracing his host, said such strange things, thanking him for the favor of having dubbed him a knight, that it is impossible to hit upon the right way to tell them.

o: El ventero, por verle ya fuera de la venta, con no menos retóricas, aunque con más breves palabras, respondió a las suyas, y, sin pedirle la costa de la posada, le dejó ir a la buen hora.
t: The innkeeper, seeing him already outside the inn, replied to his words with no less rhetoric, though in briefer terms, and, without asking which way to the inn, let him go his way.
